newsitem.title: USA: Brown family needs funds for Simpson custody battle.
newsitem.headline: Brown family needs funds for Simpson custody battle.

text.p: A friend of Nicole Brown Simpson's parents said on Friday the family could no longer pay their legal bills in the custody fight for O.J. Simpson's two young children and appealed to the public to help wage the fight.

Gloria Allred, a Los Angeles lawyer and friend of the Brown family, made the appeal at a news conference on behalf of Louis and Juditha Brown, who have been drained of money by the custody battle and were forced to dismiss their lawyers.

"The custody trial is scheduled to begin next month and therefore this appeal is urgent. They need the public's assistance now," Allred said on the lawn of the Santa Monica courthouse where the Browns are suing O.J. Simpson in a separate wrongful death lawsuit.

The former football star and television pitchman was found not guilty last year of the murder of his ex-wife Nicole and her friend Ronald Goldman. But the Brown and the Goldman families are now suing Simpson in civil court.

Allred said that although the Browns were in "significant need of money to hire a lawyer" in the custody case, their financial woes would not affect their ability to fight the civil case against Simpson, in which they are asking for hefty damages.
The family has retained two lawyers in that case in which a jury is now being selected.

But with the departure of the custody lawyers, the Browns are now representing themselves in battle for custody of their grandchildren, Sydney, 10, and Justin, 8. O.J. Simpson agreed to grant temporary custody to the Browns while he was jailed and on trial, but once acquitted he sought to regain full custody.

Eleanor Stegmeier, one of the lawyers who had been representing the Browns, confirmed on Friday that she was off the case. But she said that news reports about the amount of legal fees were "grossly inaccurate."

The Orange County Register reported Friday that Eleanor Stegmeier and Saul Gelbart were removed from the case after amassing fees totalling more than $100,000 in a recent pre-trial hearing that lasted nine days. That hearing failed to resolve the custody matter, which is set to go to trial next month.

Allred, who has previously represented the Brown family on matters related to the murder trial, kicked off the fundraising effort with a check for $1,000. She said it was not a "viable option" for her to represent the Browns in the custody trial.
